- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., > 0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5), model underestimates; increase forecast by 2–5% to account for potential rebound.  
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes in sentiment; apply a 1–3 day lag correction to avoid immediate overshoot.  
- If forecast shows sharp upward trend after a spike, reduce peak by 5–10% to reflect mean reversion tendency.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 3–5 days of history show strong upward momentum, model often overestimates; apply downward bias of 3–7% to align with true mean reversion.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated oscillations (e.g., alternating +/–0.3), model tends to misalign with true volatility; use sentiment-weighted smoothing to dampen overfitting.
